key_concepts: Genotype is the genetic makeup inherited from parents
Phenotype is the observable trait determined by genotype and environment
Alleles are different versions of a gene
Homozygous means having two identical alleles; heterozygous means having two different all
Dominant alleles mask recessive alleles in heterozygous individuals
A cross between two heterozygous individuals gives a 1:2:1 genotypic ratio
Punnett squares are used to predict genotypic and phenotypic ratios of offspring
Monohybrid crosses involve one gene with two alleles
Dihybrid crosses involve two genes and predict combinations of two traits
Environmental factors such as sunlight and diet can influence phenotype
Common human traits such as eye color, hair color, and blood type can be inherited
Probability can be used to predict the traits of future offspring
